title: per-request-provenance-and-fairshare-billing-for-composite-embeddings-and-toolcalls
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem statement: Composite, non-chat requests that include embeddings, rerank, and structured tool invocations are currently being billed in a way that can over- or under-charge customers when speculative prefetch, parallelism, partial failures, retries, or downstream tool fallbacks occur. Quotas and rate limits are consumed at different points in the pipeline (reservation vs commit) which leads to quota leakage during retries and noisy spikes in usage-based billing reconciliation.

Scope: This ticket designs and implements a per-request provenance and fair-share billing model for composite calls (embeddings + rerank + toolcalls + structured output). It covers: (1) tagging request provenance end-to-end, (2) implementing commit/rollback semantics for quota reservations, (3) deterministic attribution rules for shared-prefetch and speculative calls, (4) idempotency and replay-safe metering ledger entries, (5) refund/credit mechanics for partial-failures, and (6) dashboards and audits to validate correctness.

Non-goals: Changes to chat endpoint metering; deep changes to pricing model. This work focuses on accuracy and quota correctness for non-chat composite endpoints and toolcall paths.
acceptance_criteria: All composite requests contain an immutable provenance token that is passed to downstream services and recorded in the metering ledger
Quota reservation API implements reserve/commit/cancel semantics and prevents permanent quota consumption on transient retries
Shared speculative prefetches are attributed deterministically to a single logical request origin or split via configurable fair-share rules, with a clear audit trail
Billing discrepancies for embeddings+rerank+toolchains drop to <0.1% of daily volume in staging compared to baseline disagreement metric
Automated integration tests cover: retry scenarios, partial tool failure with fallback, idempotent replay, and refund issuance flow
Dashboard surfaces per-request lineage and a histogram of attribution decision outcomes for the last 30 days
Migration path and rollout plan validated on staging with canary at 5% before 100% production rollout

updates: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after customer support escalation and internal audit showing 1.7% daily discrepancy for composite endpoints.
2026-03-03: Spike kickoff complete. Mapped 7 distinct code paths where embeddings are prefetched or reused; identified two places where quota is consumed on reservation only.
2026-03-06: Design review with PM and Legal. Decision: provenance token must be opaque, single string, TTL 24 hours, and stored in ledger entries for 90 days for auditability.
2026-03-08: Prototypeed reserve/commit/cancel HTTP endpoints and smoke-tested against staging traffic; observed a race where concurrent commits double-apply for shared-prefetch case.

2026-03-10: Deterministic attribution algorithm agreed: prefer the originating request if available, else hash(fanout_parent_id + service) to pick deterministic owner; fallback policy is round-robin fair-share with configurable weights.
2026-03-12: First PR opened that implements provenance header propagation and ledger writes. Integration tests failing in CI due to test expectation mismatch on refund timing — investigating.
2026-03-14: Fixed refund timing race by deferring ledger finalization until commit window closes or commit received; tests updated. Preparing canary plan and dashboards for tomorrow's SRE sync.
tests: Unit tests for reserve/commit/cancel semantics (race conditions + idempotency token coverage)
Integration test that simulates: request -> speculative prefetch -> primary success, tool fallback -> partial failure -> refund issuance
Load test to validate rate limiter integration with reservation (100k composite requests/hour) and ensure no quota leakage under burst retries
Reconciliation test: synthetic workload run to ensure billing ledger agrees with per-customer token counts within <0.1% after 24-hour reconcile
rollout_plan: Deploy ledger + reservation API to staging and enable provenance header for 100% staging traffic
Run synthetic reconciler daily for 3 days and validate discrepancy metric <0.1%
Canary: enable on production 5% of requests with circuit breaker to revert on anomaly
Expand to 25% after 48 hours if no anomalies; run reconciliation and manual spot checks
Full rollout to 100% with monitoring gates and post-deployment retrospective
metrics: billing_discrepancy_rate: fraction of customer-days with >0.5% disagreement (target <0.1%)
quota_leak_events_per_hour: incidents where reserved quota not committed or cancelled (target 0)
refund_latency_seconds: time from partial-failure detection to refund issuance (target <60s median)
attribution_decision_entropy: measure of nondeterminism in attribution (target: decrease by 90%)
